Job Description

Work Arrangement:

Hybrid: This internship is categorized as on-site. The selected intern is expected to report to the office 3 days a week.

Location:

Sunnyvale, CA

About the Team

The State Estimation, Alignment, and Mapping (SEAM) team develops the sensing and spatial understanding capabilities that help autonomous vehicles know where they are, interpret their surroundings, and maintain reliable operation over time. The team works on sensor fusion, state estimation, real-time localization, static and dynamic sensor calibration, next-generation mapping, and capabilities that support primary and fallback driving systems.

SEAM combines robotics, computer vision, estimation theory, machine learning, geometry, and production software engineering. Our work supports both onboard, real-time autonomy and offboard, high-fidelity map and data-generation workflows.

About the Role

As a SEAM Intern, you will work on a well-scoped research or engineering project related to sensing, estimation, localization, mapping, or autonomy reliability. You will collaborate with experienced engineers and researchers to design algorithms, implement software, evaluate system performance, and understand how sensing capabilities operate in real-world autonomous driving systems.

Potential focus areas include:

- State Estimation and Sensor Fusion: Combine information from multiple sensors and vehicle signals to estimate position, orientation, motion, and other states robustly.
- Sensor Alignment and Calibration: Develop methods for static and dynamic calibration, sensor registration, and maintaining alignment as vehicle and environmental conditions change.
- Localization: Improve real-time localization and map-based positioning across diverse driving environments.
- Next-Generation Mapping: Build or evaluate high-fidelity, large-scale maps that provide useful spatial context beyond the immediate sensor range.
- Fallback and Secondary Capabilities: Develop reliable estimation, localization, or mapping functions that support safe operation when nominal system capabilities are unavailable or degraded.

What You’ll Do

- Develop, prototype, and evaluate algorithms for sensor fusion, state estimation, localization, calibration, mapping, or related autonomy capabilities.
- Work with camera, lidar, radar, inertial, vehicle, map, and other multimodal data sources.
- Implement software and tools for data processing, visualization, offline analysis, simulation, and system evaluation.
- Analyze accuracy, robustness, latency, and failure modes across diverse operating conditions.
- Apply software engineering best practices, including design reviews, code reviews, automated testing, continuous integration, and documentation.
- Collaborate with perception, planning, controls, robotics, systems engineering, and vehicle-program partners.
- Communicate technical findings and contribute to design discussions and project documentation.

Required Qualifications

- Currently enrolled in or pursuing a Ph.D. degree in Robotics, Computer Science, Electrical Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Applied Mathematics, or a related technical field.
- Demonstrated experience through coursework, research, academic projects, or professional work in robotics, state estimation, sensor fusion, computer vision, localization, mapping, controls, or a related area.
- Strong programming skills in C++ and/or Python.
- Strong foundation in linear algebra, probability, geometry, optimization, or estimation methods.
- Strong analytical and problem-solving skills.
- Ability to work collaboratively in a cross-functional, team-oriented environment.
- Strong written, verbal, and presentation skills.
- Availability to work full-time, 40 hours per week, during the internship period.

Preferred Qualifications

- Experience with Kalman filtering, factor graphs, SLAM, visual-inertial odometry, bundle adjustment, point clouds, geometric computer vision, or multi-sensor calibration.
- Familiarity with autonomous vehicles, advanced driver assistance systems, robotics, ROS, or safety-critical systems.
- Experience with large-scale sensor or map datasets, simulation, data association, or offline evaluation.
- Experience with machine learning frameworks such as PyTorch, TensorFlow, or JAX.
- Familiarity with real-time systems, distributed systems, high-performance computing, or production software development
- Intent to return to a degree program after completion of the internship or co-op.

About Cowboy Space Corp.

Mission
Cowboy Space Corporation is solving the global energy crisis by building the infrastructure for abundant, resilient space-based solar energy. We are tackling one of humanity's most complex engineering challenges with a world-class team dedicated to delivering a revolutionary power platform. Cowboy Space Corporation is transforming how civilization powers, computes and connects - from orbit to Earth.

Background
Cowboy Space Corporation is building the infrastructure to power and connect the orbital economy. Our modular, scalable satellites collect sunlight in Low Earth Orbit to enable multiple integrated applications: transmitting energy via infrared lasers (space-to-earth and space-to-space), powering on-orbit high-performance computing clusters (GPU/TPU), and providing secure, high bandwidth optical data transport.

Current energy and data systems rely on complex logistics and outdated infrastructure. Cowboy Space Corporation overcomes these challenges by enabling direct, on-demand, secure, and scalable energy distribution and data processing from space. This will revolutionize how we operate in orbit and on Earth, supporting the rapidly expanding space industrial base, ISAM (In-Space Servicing, Assembly, and Manufacturing) operations, remote regions, and military bases.

Baiju Bhatt founded Cowboy Space Corporation in 2024. Inspired by his father's work with NASA Langley Research Center, Baiju earned his B.S. in Physics and M.S. in Mathematics at Stanford before co-founding Robinhood, now a public company that has helped over 20 million Americans access the financial system. Cowboy Space Corporation has raised ~$365 million from Index Ventures, Interlagos, Construct Ventures, Breakthrough Energy Ventures, Andreessen Horowitz, NEA, and others.

This is an ambitious mission that demands extraordinary talent. Cowboy Space Corporation's team has worked at places like SpaceX, Blue Origin, Stoke Space, Astranis and NASA, and is based in San Carlos, CA. If you're ready to solve complex technical challenges and help build the most important energy company in the world, we want to hear from you.

Responsibilities

- Design, development, and testing of software across flight, embedded, and ground systems, including avionics, guidance/navigation/control, and satellite bus/payload software

- Build and maintain software for signal processing, RF/optical communication pipelines, and on-orbit compute infrastructure (GPU/TPU clusters)

- Develop tooling and services for mission operations, telemetry/command infrastructure, and satellite health monitoring

- Write, test, and debug code across the stack — from low-level embedded/real-time systems to higher-level ground and data systems

- Collaborate with hardware, electrical, and systems engineering teams to define interfaces, debug integration issues, and validate end-to-end system behavior

- Build simulation, test, and hardware-in-the-loop frameworks to validate software against spacecraft requirements

- Participate in code reviews, write technical documentation, and contribute to engineering best practices as the team and codebase scale

Basic Qualifications

- Currently enrolled as an undergraduate or graduate student in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Electrical Engineering, or a related STEM field

- Strong fundamentals in software engineering: data structures, algorithms, and computer architecture

- Proficiency in at least one systems or general-purpose programming language (C, C++, Python, or similar)

- Collaborative, self-directed work style; comfort with ambiguity and learning quickly

Preferred Qualifications

- Experience with embedded or real-time systems programming (RTOS, bare-metal, or similar constrained environments)

- Exposure to signal processing, hardware description languages (VHDL/Verilog), or FPGA-based development

- Familiarity with flight software frameworks (e.g., cFS, F Prime) or spacecraft software architectures

- Experience with version control, CI/CD pipelines, and automated testing frameworks

- Prior internship, coursework, or personal project experience involving robotics, satellites, avionics, or other hardware-adjacent software

- Comfort debugging across the hardware/software boundary, including use of tools like oscilloscopes, logic analyzers, or debuggers

Compensation

About Zipline

Zipline is the world’s largest and most experienced drone delivery service. We are on a mission to serve all humans equally by ensuring access to food, medicine and essential goods anytime, anywhere. We design, build, and operate the world’s largest autonomous logistics system, delivering critical supplies quickly and reliably. Today, Zipline operates on four continents, makes a delivery somewhere in the world every 30 seconds, and has completed millions of deliveries to date, including blood, vaccines, medical supplies, food, and retail products.

Our customers include the world’s largest and most prominent healthcare systems, governments, retailers, restaurants and global businesses who rely on us to save lives, reduce emissions, increase economic opportunity, and provide delivery from point A to point B as fast as possible. The drone is only 15% of what we’ve built to enable seamless, reliable, global operations.

Our system strengthens supply chains, reduces congestion, and gives people time back. With more than 140 million commercial autonomous miles safely flown, Zipline is redefining access to healthcare, consumer products, and food across the globe.

We operate at a global scale and are looking for practical problem solvers who thrive on real-world challenges and rapid growth. Our team is motivated by building systems that have a direct, meaningful impact on people’s lives and by scaling the future of logistics. We are seeking people who sculpt from first principles, enjoy facing adversity, and can do the impossible at record breaking speeds.

About the Operations Experience Team

The way people experience a company isn't defined by one big moment—it's shaped by hundreds of small ones. The first day on the job. A leader's message after a major milestone. An All Hands that leaves you excited about where the company is going. Those moments don't happen by accident.

Operations Experience exists to design those moments with intention. We partner with leaders across Operations to build the communications, systems, and experiences that help people feel informed, engaged, and inspired as the organization grows. One day we might be designing a leadership experience, the next we could be reimagining onboarding, creating a new communications strategy, planning an event or recognition moment, or building tools that make it easier for teams to find the information they need. You’ll work closely with the Head of Operations Experience and cross-functional partners, learning how strategy moves from an idea to a fully executed experience in a fast-moving environment.

- Has a strong eye for design, organization, and content quality, with an instinct for creating work that is thoughtful, polished, and intuitive.

About the Role

The Speculative Decoding team at Together AI builds the draft models and algorithms that let large language models generate faster without changing their outputs. Our speculators run in production on frontier open models such as DeepSeek, Kimi and GLM. Our work sits at the intersection of model training, inference algorithms and serving systems, and we co-design all three to lower the cost and latency of generation.

As a research intern, you will dive into open questions in speculative decoding: new drafter architectures and verification schemes, knowledge distillation and training recipes that align draft and target models, and drafters that adapt as traffic shifts. You will train and fine-tune draft models at scale on dedicated GPU clusters, and test your ideas against realistic serving workloads, including long-context and agentic traffic.

Projects aim to answer important research questions in speculative decoding, enabling faster generation on frontier models, drafters that keep pace with changing workloads, and robust, reproducible evaluation under real traffic.

Past Research

Speculative decoding research by Together researchers, interns and academic collaborators includes:

- Speculative Speculative Decoding (ICLR 2026)

- When RL Meets Adaptive Speculative Training: A Unified Training-Serving System (ICML 2026)

- Beat the Long Tail: Distribution-Aware Speculative Decoding for RL Training (MLSys 2026)

Responsibilities

- Research and prototype new efficient speculative decoding algorithms and draft model architectures

- Train, fine-tune and distill draft models, and design rigorous experiments to validate hypotheses.

- Implement optimized version for serving engines to show efficacy in real world workloads

- Communicate the plans, progress, and results of projects to the broader team

- Share findings through technical write-ups and blog posts, and help bring successful ideas into production

Requirements

- Currently pursuing a Master's or Ph.D. degree in Computer Science, Electrical Engineering, or a related field

- Strong knowledge of Machine Learning and Deep Learning fundamentals

- Hands-on experience training or fine-tuning large models with distributed training frameworks (e.g., Megatron-LM, FSDP)

- Familiarity with modern model architectures, such as Mixture-of-Experts and hybrid attention

Preferred Qualifications

- Prior research experience in speculative decoding, efficient inference, or efficient machine learning

- Publications at leading conferences in machine learning or systems (e.g., NeurIPS, ICML, ICLR, MLSys)

- Experience with knowledge distillation, post-training, or reinforcement learning

- Familiarity with LLM serving engines (e.g., vLLM, SGLang, TensorRT-LLM)

- Contributions to open-source machine learning projects

About Zipline

Zipline is the world’s largest and most experienced drone delivery service. We are on a mission to serve all humans equally by ensuring access to food, medicine and essential goods anytime, anywhere. We design, build, and operate the world’s largest autonomous logistics system, delivering critical supplies quickly and reliably. Today, Zipline operates on four continents, makes a delivery somewhere in the world every 30 seconds, and has completed millions of deliveries to date, including blood, vaccines, medical supplies, food, and retail products.

Our customers include the world’s largest and most prominent healthcare systems, governments, retailers, restaurants and global businesses who rely on us to save lives, reduce emissions, increase economic opportunity, and provide delivery from point A to point B as fast as possible. The drone is only 15% of what we’ve built to enable seamless, reliable, global operations.

Our system strengthens supply chains, reduces congestion, and gives people time back. With more than 140 million commercial autonomous miles safely flown, Zipline is redefining access to healthcare, consumer products, and food across the globe.

We operate at a global scale and are looking for practical problem solvers who thrive on real-world challenges and rapid growth. Our team is motivated by building systems that have a direct, meaningful impact on people’s lives and by scaling the future of logistics. We are seeking people who sculpt from first principles, enjoy facing adversity, and can do the impossible at record breaking speeds.

About the Flight Test Engineering Team

Zipline’s Flight Test Engineering team is a specialized group that designs flight test courses and methods to support our overall system validation progress. This involves developing custom flight control software for complex maneuvers and collaborating with development engineers to design rigorous tests for all critical edge cases.

We leverage expertise in system design, statistics, flight physics, and sound experimental methods to ensure our flight tests are effective and safe. The team partners closely with Controls and Dynamics, Embedded Software, Autonomy, Systems Engineering, Powertrain, Structure, and Flight Operations teams to build comprehensive test plans and test cards.

Our work spans simulation, hardware testing, data-driven analysis, and system-level evaluations that support deployments across the globe. As an intern, you’ll collaborate with engineers across these domains, gaining hands-on exposure to how industry-leading autonomous systems are designed, tested, and validated at scale.

The Role

As a Flight Test Engineering Intern, you will be instrumental in analyzing flight test data logs to determine test effectiveness, identify success/failure root causes, and track performance trends.

You will also directly contribute to the design of new flight test campaigns, collaborating with other engineers to define the test scope, test method, and data post-processing.

This is a unique opportunity for someone excited to learn how complex robotic systems are validated, who enjoys problem-solving, and who wants to build real-world experience working with autonomy software, data analysis, and systems engineering.

What You'll Do

- Analyze flight test data logs using custom scripts (Python, DataBricks, SQL) to identify anomalies, assess reliability, track performance trends, and perform regression analyses.

- Design, oversee the execution, and review the results of software validation and flight test campaigns to ensure new features perform as intended and prevent hardware/software regression.

- Daily test and monitor the develop branch to quickly surface instability and potential future issues.

- Collaborate with cross-functional partners (GNC, Aerodynamics, Structures, Systems Engineering) to ensure system-level requirements (e.g., acceleration, range, climb rate) are clear, measurable, and that vehicle changes are mature for flight testing.

- Define or develop novel test infrastructure, including application-based tools to support flight testing, new instrumentation systems (e.g., load cells, vision systems). or modified flight control software, to collect auxiliary data in flight.

- Establish and maintain documentation, dashboards, and SQL search queries to track test progress and operational efficiency.

- Be ready to directly own any aspect of flight operations (preflight, launch, flight maneuvers, incident reporting) or supervise these activities with the flight operations team.

What You'll Bring

- You must have completed the second year of your undergraduate studies in physics, mathematics, mechanical, aerospace, system engineering, computer science, electrical engineering or related fields. Masters and PhD students are also eligible.

- Strong mathematical and physics background.

- Experience in autonomous vehicle/ robotic system integration and testing work.

- Experience in data process, visualization.

About Akuna

Akuna Capital is an innovative trading firm with a strong focus on collaboration, cutting-edge technology, data-driven solutions, and automation. We specialize in providing liquidity on a variety of exchanges across various asset classes, primarily as an options market maker. To do this successfully, we build and maintain our own low-latency technologies, including application frameworks, trading strategies, and mathematical models.

Our Founding Partners first conceptualized Akuna in their hometown of Sydney, Australia. They opened the firm’s first office in 2011 in the heart of the derivatives industry and the options capital of the world – Chicago. Today, Akuna is proud to operate from additional offices around the world: Sydney, Shanghai, Singapore, and London.

What You’ll Do as an Entry-Level C++ Software Engineer at Akuna

C++ software engineers at Akuna have the opportunity to work on a variety of high-performance systems that power the firm’s core business operations. Our engineers work on small-to-medium-sized teams that frequently interface with Quant and Trading, allowing them to build expertise in a specific domain area while maintaining broader exposure to the needs of their end-users. Akuna’s C++ systems are heavily multithreaded, asynchronous, and distributed by nature, which comes with a slew of challenges; our engineers are tasked with ensuring these systems are reliable, efficient, scalable, and flexible enough for even the most niche use cases. Entry-level engineers in particular are responsible for day-to-day upkeep of core systems, servicing lower-risk feature requests, and executing individual projects on behalf of their team’s stakeholders.

Akuna is looking for software engineers who are motivated, can solve complex problems, and are willing to reach for creative solutions when faced with novel problems. We value innovation, hard work, and knowledge, and we want our engineers to make a direct impact on the firm. Whether you are interested in algorithms and data structures, concurrency, networking and protocols, performance tuning, data capture and analysis, mathematical modeling, hardware, or something else, there’s engaging work to be done.

Requirements for This Role

- Pursuing a bachelor’s, master’s, or Ph.D. in a technical field (computer science/engineering, math, physics, or equivalent)

- Graduating by August 2027

- Legal authorization to work in the U.S. as of the first day of employment, including F-1 students using OPT or STEM

Previous experience in finance or trading is not required. Many of our engineers joined Akuna with little-to-no prior knowledge of the markets, and we pride ourselves on our ability to onboard those new to the industry. Training and continuous education are provided for all engineers to ensure they can build the requisite technical and non-technical skillset for success.

Qualities That Make a Great C++ Software Engineer Candidate

- Experience programming in modern C++ (C++20 or later; C++23 preferred)

- Experience with several of the following

- Distributed systems

- Parallel processing

- Asynchronous architectures

- Networking or protocol encoding/decoding

- Lock-free data structures and algorithms

- Performance profiling (e.g. perf, gprof, vtune)

- Scripting, such as in Python or shell

- Familiarity with standard debugging tools (e.g. GDB, Valgrind, address sanitizer)

- The ability to effectively communicate with non-technical stakeholders in Quant and Trading to obtain requirements, workshop solutions, and implement agreed-upon roadmaps

- The ability to react quickly and effectively to rapidly changing market conditions, including the ability to quickly and accurately respond and/or solve math and coding problems, is an essential function of the role

- A passion for building complex systems from the ground up

- The ability to collaborate with other developers of different backgrounds, specialties, and knowledge levels to collectively deliver cohesive solutions to non-trivial problems

- An intrinsically motivated attitude and the ability to work independently

- A strong sense of ownership, including a drive to fix bugs when they inevitably arise

In addition to the above technical skills, Akuna values diversity of experience and perspective. We believe that engineers with varied backgrounds and interests allow us to approach problems from unique angles and to uncover innovative, optimal solutions. We want everyone to feel empowered to apply; we welcome your application, and we strongly encourage you to take the first steps in joining us in the future!

Resumes must be submitted in PDF format.

By applying to this role, you are indicating this is your top preference and acknowledge you will not be considered for other Quant and/or Tech roles at Akuna this recruiting season. This acknowledgement does not limit applications to Trading roles - in addition to this role, you may apply to any Trader roles of interest.

Our interview process is designed to evaluate your individual skills and judgment, and the use of AI tools will result in disqualification from the hiring process.

With teams in Denver, San Francisco, and New York, we support more than 500,000 small businesses nationwide and are building a workplace that reflects the people we serve.

All full-time employees receive competitive base pay, benefits, and equity (RSUs) — because everyone who helps build Gusto should share in its success. Offer amounts are determined by role, level, and location. Learn more about our Total Rewards philosophy.

AI is a fundamental part of how work gets done at Gusto. We expect all team members to actively engage with AI tools relevant to their role and grow their fluency as the technology evolves. AI experience requirements vary by role and will be assessed during the interview process.

About the Role:

As a Finance Intern on Gusto’s Finance, BizOps & Strategy (FBOS) team, you’ll spend 12 weeks working on real projects that shape how we run the business. You’ll support leaders in Customer Experience, EPD, and Corporate Development, helping turn financial data into decisions about margin, cost to serve, and resourcing. Day to day, that means building financial reports, analyzing costs to find savings, and partnering with teams across Gusto on projects that move the team’s roadmap forward. Along the way, you’ll use AI tools and automation to work faster and go deeper than a traditional finance internship allows.

You’ll be paired with a dedicated mentor and a team manager who will support you from onboarding through your final presentation. By the end of the summer, you’ll have seen firsthand how finance works as a true partner to the business.

Please note: We’ll be offering only one cohort start and end date (Cohort 1: May 17, 2027 - August 6, 2027).

Deadline to Apply: Monday, October 26th at 4:00 pm PST

About the Team:

You'll join Gusto's Finance, BizOps & Strategy (FBOS) team, which provides financial, operational, and strategic support at the corporate, department, and product level as we scale to serve even more customers. Our partners sit directly inside business orgs like Customer Experience, EPD, and Corporate Development, translating financial data into operating decisions on margin, cost to serve, and resourcing. As Gusto evolves into an AI native company, we're using automation, predictive insights, and smarter data systems to define and defend our business model while accelerating growth. As a Finance Intern, you'll see firsthand how finance works as a true partner to the business rather than a back office function.

Here’s what you’ll do day-to-day:

- Work cross-functionally on high-impact projects that use data, automation, and AI-powered tools

- Build and maintain recurring financial/operational reporting for your partner org

- Analyze cost or margin drivers and summarize findings for non-finance stakeholders

- Support a defined roadmap project end-to-end alongside your mentor

- Partner with CX/EPD/Corp Dev counterparts on data requests and ad hoc analysis

Here’s what we're looking for:

- Rising junior or senior (entering your 3rd or 4th year after this internship)

- Demonstrates genuine interest in financial trends, technology innovation, and applying classroom knowledge to real business challenges

- Comfortable working in Excel/Google Sheets; curious about how AI tools can speed up analysis work

- Strong attention to detail and the ability to communicate findings clearly to non-finance stakeholders

- Self-starter, comfortable with ambiguity in a fast-paced environment

Our cash compensation amount for this role is $32.70/hr for undergraduate students in Denver and $42.07/hr for undergraduate students in New York.

At Gusto, we don't use titles the traditional way, as a signal of rank or hierarchy. Instead, our titles describe two things at once — your craft (what you do, e.g. Engineering, Design) and your scope of ownership (what you're accountable for) — which is why you'll see something like "Head of X" instead of a rank word like "Director" that tells you neither. Our customers come from all walks of life and so do we. We hire great people from a wide variety of backgrounds, not just because it's the right thing to do, but because it makes our company stronger. If you share our values and our enthusiasm for small businesses, you will find a home at Gusto.

About Zipline

Zipline is the world’s largest and most experienced drone delivery service. We are on a mission to serve all humans equally by ensuring access to food, medicine and essential goods anytime, anywhere. We design, build, and operate the world’s largest autonomous logistics system, delivering critical supplies quickly and reliably. Today, Zipline operates on four continents, makes a delivery somewhere in the world every 30 seconds, and has completed millions of deliveries to date, including blood, vaccines, medical supplies, food, and retail products.

Our customers include the world’s largest and most prominent healthcare systems, governments, retailers, restaurants and global businesses who rely on us to save lives, reduce emissions, increase economic opportunity, and provide delivery from point A to point B as fast as possible. The drone is only 15% of what we’ve built to enable seamless, reliable, global operations.

Our system strengthens supply chains, reduces congestion, and gives people time back. With more than 140 million commercial autonomous miles safely flown, Zipline is redefining access to healthcare, consumer products, and food across the globe.

We operate at a global scale and are looking for practical problem solvers who thrive on real-world challenges and rapid growth. Our team is motivated by building systems that have a direct, meaningful impact on people’s lives and by scaling the future of logistics. We are seeking people who sculpt from first principles, enjoy facing adversity, and can do the impossible at record breaking speeds.

About the Operations Experience Team

The way people experience a company isn't defined by one big moment—it's shaped by hundreds of small ones. The first day on the job. A leader's message after a major milestone. An All Hands that leaves you excited about where the company is going. Those moments don't happen by accident.

Operations Experience exists to design those moments with intention. We partner with leaders across Operations to build the communications, systems, and experiences that help people feel informed, engaged, and inspired as the organization grows. One day we might be designing a leadership experience, the next we could be reimagining onboarding, creating a new communications strategy, planning an event or recognition moment, or building tools that make it easier for teams to find the information they need. We love turning ideas into experiences and bringing order to complexity. Above all, we believe the details matter in every moment.

The Role

As an Operations Experience Intern, you’ll work on real projects across internal communications, events, onboarding, employee engagement, and the systems we use to keep teams connected. You may help build a new employee experience, organize information so it is easier to find, support an Operations event, develop communications, or turn an idea into a polished resource that teams can actually use. Your work will contribute directly to shaping an Operations experience that grows alongside the organization. You’ll work closely with the Head of Operations Experience and cross-functional partners, learning how strategy moves from an idea to a fully executed experience in a fast-moving environment.

What You'll Do

- Support the development and execution of Operations communications, including drafting, editing, designing content, and ensuring information is clear, consistent, and actionable.

- Plan and create employee experiences across All Hands, events, offsites, onboarding, and other culture-building moments.

- Partner on the organization and innovation of internal resources and information systems, including digital workplace pages, communication calendars, design, and planning tools.

- Assist with event and program planning from idea through execution, including timelines, logistics, communications, materials, and follow-up.

- Conduct research, gather feedback, and help identify opportunities to make Operations experiences simpler and more engaging.

- Learn how to manage projects across multiple stakeholders, balance strategy with execution, and build repeatable systems that can scale with a growing organization.

What You'll Bring

- You must have completed the second year of a bachelor’s degree, with an interest in communications, business, operations, employee experience, organizational design, or a related field. Master’s are also eligible.

- Strong written and verbal communication skills, with an ability to turn information into clear, concise, and engaging content.

- Has a strong eye for design, organization, and content quality, with an instinct for creating work that is thoughtful, polished, and intuitive.

- Excellent organization and attention to detail, including comfort managing multiple projects, deadlines, and moving pieces at once.

- Demonstrates exceptional professionalism, discretion, and judgment, with the confidence to work alongside senior leaders and represent Operations Experience in high-visibility settings.

- Ability to work onsite in our South San Francisco office 5 days a week (full time).

What Else You Should Know

This internship is a full-time position, in-person at our South San Francisco office. We will host our Spring 2027 interns from spring (January 2027 - April 2027). Zipline is unable to sponsor work visas for applicants to this position.

The hourly rate for this internship is $34 per hour. Additional benefits may include relocation support, a housing stipend, overtime pay, paid sick time, and other benefits, where applicable and subject to local requirements.

Candidates are limited to three (3) applications within a 30-day period.

Zipline is an equal opportunity employer and prohibits discrimination and harassment of any type without regard to race, color, religion, age, sex, national origin, disability status, genetics, protected veteran status, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, or any other characteristic protected by federal, state or local laws or our own sensibilities.

Zipline is also committed to providing reasonable accommodations to individuals with disabilities. Please let your point of contact at Zipline know if you require any accommodations throughout your interview process.

We are looking for talented individuals to join us for an internship. PhD internships at Our Company provide students with the opportunity to actively contribute to our products and research, as well as to the organization's future plans and emerging technologies.

- Strong software engineering fundamentals: clean, testable code, version control, and the ability to debug complex systems end to end.
- Proficient in Python and at least one deep learning framework such as PyTorch or TensorFlow.
Strong problem-solving ability, a collaborative mindset, and a genuine interest in applying AI to real-world products.

- Open-source contributions, strong results in ML competitions (Kaggle, Tianchi, ACM/ICPC), or granted patents.

Risepoint is an education technology company that helps regional universities launch and grow online programs for modern learners. Risepoint supports more than 100 universities and colleges across five countries, with programs concentrated in high-demand fields including nursing, healthcare, teaching, business, technology, and public service. Our suite of products and services supports the full student journey and each university’s long-term goals. Together, we increase access to affordable education that delivers a strong return on investment for learners and meets employer and community needs. Learn more at risepoint.com.

The Impact You Will Make

We're investing deliberately in the transformation layer: standardized semantic layer components, clear metric definitions, and documented models that hold up as the business grows. This co-op is a real seat in that work and carries with it the opportunity to make material impact on strategy and business outcomes.

You'll sit between analysis and engineering: building and standardizing the data models and semantic layer components that let our analytics leaders ship validated, governed data products faster.

This role will serve as a working liaison between Student Success Center (SSC) Analytics and our Business Technology team. You will translate what the business needs into something technically sound and communicate what's possible back into something operators can act on. This role provides you with the opportunity to work cohesively between the data and analytics layer.

Co-op Duration

This opportunity runs from January 2027 through June 2027, with some flexibility on start and end to

accommodate academic schedules.

Weekly Schedule

This is a full-time co-op experience, 40 hours per week, Monday through Friday, designed to provide

hands-on, real-world exposure.

How You Will Bring Our Mission to Life

What You Will Do

- Design and build data models in Databricks that consolidate scattered logic into a defensible source of truth for our student success center (SSC) reporting and analysis.

- Standardize semantic layer components and metric definitions so operational metrics mean one thing in every report, dashboard, and leadership deck.

- Improve data quality at the transformation layer — validation, freshness, and reconciliation checks, so we find problems before a leader does.

- Partner with Business Technology on upstream data sources, pipeline changes, and governance, acting as the connective tissue between the two teams.

- Turn a recurring manual report into a modeled data product in Power BI that maintains itself, then quantify the hours you gave back.

- Document what you build — lineage, definitions, and the reasoning, so it's usable by someone who wasn't in the room. Contribute new documentation for existing deliverables, ensure consistency across documentation, and simplify the overall approach while retaining context.

- Recommend, don't just execute. When you see a better way to model something, we want to hear it, and we'll give you room to try it.

What Success Looks Like

- Two or three core SSC data models are built, documented, and trusted enough that analysts query them instead of rewriting the logic themselves.

- Contribute meaningfully to our semantic layer for our most used operational metrics

- Coordinate with stakeholders in SSC to enable better workflows, drive programmatic analytics solutions, and serve as a liaison for our SSC Analytics team.
- Adoption: how many reports and dashboards are rebuilt on the models you standardized, versus still running on one-off logic.

- Hours returned: manual report building and rework time eliminated, measured against a baseline we set in your first month.

- Net improvement of our Databricks environment specific to the catalogs and schemas that we own and manage. Measured by user feedback and adoption.

What You’ll Bring to the Team

Experience That Matters Most

- Working SQL ability. You can write joins and aggregations, follow someone else’s query, and are confident with debugging and resolving open data issues within queries, notebooks, and jobs.

- Functional Python experience. We do not require you to have advanced proficiency with Python, but have the confidence to navigate existing scripts, workflows, and understand how to approach and implement solutions with the help of AI.

- Foundational database management concepts. Keys, grains, normalization, and a basic sense of what makes a table well designed and structured.

- Strong analytical judgment and experience in a real-world business setting.

- Demonstrated experience working with ambiguity to drive measurable outcomes to stakeholders.

- Strong verbal and written communication skills across both technical and non-technical stakeholder cohorts.

Experience That’s Great to Have

- Prior experience working within a data engineering and/or analytics environment alongside others.

- Databricks, Snowflake, or any cloud data platform application knowledge and experience.

- Confidence with technical documentation and overall project management within an engineering framework.

- Applicable knowledge working with data transformation tools, application and confidence with AI-tooling in an analytics workflow, and overall confidence navigating in and out of engineering workflows.

Certa is the AI-first third-party operating system. Enterprises, from the Fortune 500 to fast-growing startups, use our no-code platform to onboard, assess, and monitor their vendors, suppliers, and partners across risk, compliance, and ESG. We have processed over 10 million entities for 100,000+ users across 120+ countries, and are backed by Fin Capital, Vertex Ventures, and Point72 Ventures.

This is a paid 6-month internship with the opportunity to transition into a full-time role at the end based on performance. You'll build the interfaces enterprise users interact with every day, shipping real features to real customers from your first sprint, with real ownership and direct mentorship from senior engineers.

What You'll Do

- Build UI components: Develop pixel-perfect, highly interactive UI components in React.

- Turn designs into code: Translate Figma designs into production-ready code, and push back when the design doesn't make sense.

- Own performance: Care about load times, re-renders, and bundle sizes.

- Collaborate on APIs: Work with backend engineers to define APIs and data contracts.

- Ship end-to-end with quality: Write component tests, maintain a high standard for code quality, and ship features end-to-end, not just the "frontend part."

What You'll Need

- JS/TS fundamentals: A solid grasp of JavaScript/TypeScript fundamentals: closures, async, and the event loop.

- React: Working knowledge of React: hooks, state management, and component lifecycle.

- Real project experience: You've shipped something real to the web (even if small) and gone beyond tutorials: thoughtful state management (what lives where and why), API integration with loading/error/auth handling, forms with client- and server-aware validation, multi-page routing (nested and protected routes, query params), or working with a component library or design system.

- Debugging & performance: You can look at a broken UI and fix it without being told where to start, and you've used browser DevTools to spot and fix a slow render.

- Quality & UX: You care about accessibility, responsiveness, and edge cases, not just happy paths, and you have opinions about UX that you're not afraid to voice.

- AI-assisted building: You use AI tools (Copilot, v0, or similar) to build faster, and know when a suggestion is right and when it's subtly wrong.

Internship Details & What You Get

- Duration: A paid 6-month internship, with the opportunity to transition to a full-time role at the end based on performance.

- Compensation: Competitive compensation, benchmarked above market for fresher roles.

- The work: Complex, high-stakes enterprise UIs - enterprise software done right - with your code shipping to real customers quickly.

- Mentorship & impact: Direct mentorship from senior engineers who push you to grow fast, and real ownership from day one.

Location

Certa is a remote-first company and we hire globally. We believe strongly in each team member working from the location that they choose. Should Certers wish to meet and work in person, they have 3 lively office locations they can travel to:

- London

- San Francisco

- Jaipur

The perfect place for Certers to collaborate, co-work, and have face-to-face meetings.

Why Certa

- Category leadership. Certa was named a Leader in the inaugural 2026 Gartner Magic Quadrant for Third-Party Risk Management Tools - recognition that we're defining the category, not following it.

- Industry recognition. We've been honored across the analyst and awards landscape, including Top Tech and Customer Value distinctions in The Hackett Group's 2026 Risk Management SolutionMap, the ProcureTech100 (Advanced AI and Risk Management categories), and Best Overall eProcurement Software in the FinTech Breakthrough Awards.

- A top place to work. Certa was named one of Forbes' Best Startup Employers in the US. We're a fast-growing company where you'll wear many hats, ship quickly, and shape decisions that matter.

- Real scale with strong backing. We've processed over 10 million entities for 100,000+ users across 120+ countries. We're well-funded by leading investors including Fin Capital, Vertex Ventures, and Point72 Ventures, on the back of an oversubscribed Series B, headed towards Series C.

We're excited to meet you!

Company:

Boeing Defense, Space & Security (BDS) is excited to provide the Assembly Mechanic Apprenticeship program in St. Louis, designed to equip aspiring mechanics with the skills and knowledge needed to thrive in a fast-paced manufacturing environment.

Boeing Defense, Space & Security is delivering the most digitally advanced, simply and efficiently produced, and intelligently supported solutions to help warfighters solve their toughest challenges. These products deliver front-line capabilities for today’s warfighter and define the future of the air wing with fixed-wing strike, training, autonomy and crewed-uncrewed teaming.

Employees are participants in a full-time company sponsored on-the-job training program. The Assembly Mechanic Apprentice program helps learners develop the skills needed to work in a fast-paced manufacturing environment. Assignments are structured to provide learning experiences that lead to a course completion within a skill area.

The apprenticeship has 4 pathways: Structural, Electrical, Mechanical, and Composites.

The Composites cohort is a 12-week program. Upon completion the candidate will have successfully demonstrated the knowledge, skills, and ability to perform the work of a Composites Assembly Mechanic, to include, interpreting model-based drawings and blueprints, following work instructions, working with high-performance materials like fiberglass, carbon fiber, and epoxy resins, honeycomb and identifying all required hand tools, parts and equipment to accomplish defect-free work and ensuring structural integrity and safety. This involves understanding composite layup techniques, curing processes, and surface finishing, with a focus on quality control and precision.

What is a Technical Apprenticeship?

Boeing Technical Apprenticeship Program (BTAP), is an official registered apprenticeship recognized by the Department of Labor (DOL). It is an earn and learn program including formal learning, on-the-job experiences, and mentorship. Every graduate of a Registered Apprenticeship program will receive a nationally-recognized credential from the DOL.

What makes a great Technical Apprentice?

A degree is not required to apply for most technical apprenticeship programs. We select apprentices based on a range of core traits and skills, such as:

- Passion for continuously learning, improving, technology, and achieving more

- Curious mindset, problem solving, and ability to quickly apply back into your work

- Mechanical aptitude and eagerness to learn new things and help others

- Positive attitude and strong work ethic

- Ability to work independently and collaboratively with accountability to a team

- Self-motivated, with initiative and persistence in achieving success

- Strong interpersonal skills and confident communication with stakeholders

What is the experience?

As an apprentice, you'll join with other apprentices in a cohort and go through experiences together, learning Boeing, aerospace, and core Assembly fundamentals. Additionally, managers and mentors will support progress through the personal skills roadmap, learning and demonstrating new skills through hands-on application with project teams.

During the apprenticeship duration, you will initially complete a highly rigorous and accelerated learning program tailored to develop foundational skills across manufacturing and assembly. At the conclusion of the program, successful candidates will have the chance to convert to a union-represented Assembly Mechanic position where your skills will be enhanced with training and on-the-job learning tailored for a specific program.

Additional Information:

- This program is located on the St. Louis Community College – Florissant Valley campus

- Class start dates will vary based on pathway and course schedule.

- Classes may be held on first or second shift, based on demand for that session. Selected candidates will be informed of their shift prior to the start of the course

Basic Qualifications:

- High School diploma or GED

- Experience using basic math (e.g. addition, subtraction, multiplication and division)

- Basic computer experience and competency

- Able to work any shift based on the needs of the operation

Preferred Qualifications:

- Experience using basic precision measuring tools

- Experience working in a manufacturing environment

Boeing is a Drug Free Workplace where post offer applicants and employees are subject to testing for marijuana, cocaine, opioids, amphetamines, PCP, and alcohol when criteria is met as outlined in our policies.

Melius — New York City

Engineers have Cursor. Lawyers have Harvey. The office of the CFO has Ramp. Every knowledge profession has been handed a platform that lets them orchestrate agents and scale their output by an order of magnitude — except the people who actually make the things we look at, watch, and listen to.

Melius is the agents lab for creative work. We build agentic interfaces to all the work that goes into building the next generation of images, video, audio and so much more. Generative media canvas, timeline editor, asset manager, and much more, built native for agents. Using Melius, users can spend more time being creative and let go of the century old legacy tools that only acted as constraints to their imagination.

We’re backed by General Catalyst, Vine Ventures, Genius Ventures, and Antifund, and built by a team of second-time founders, former engineering leaders from Ramp, and operators who came up through top-tier VC and PE. We move fast, ship every day, and have strong opinions about craft.

The role

This is not a “summer project” internship. Expect to be treated exactly as a full time engineer would be from the first day at your job. There will be dozens of projects that you lead and are expected to educate both customers and other members of the team on.

The stack: Next.js and a real-time CRDT canvas on the frontend, NestJS / MikroORM / Postgres / Temporal / Turbopuffer on the backend, and the agent and model orchestration layer that ties it all together.

High level activities for the internship might include:

- Building new tools for our agent end-to-end — what it can do on the canvas, what it can change in the timeline editor, and how it can semantically search in the asset manager.

- Sitting in on user sessions, watching a creative hit a rough edge, and shipping the fix that same hour.

- Adding evals and traces that tell us, honestly, whether the agent got better this week.

- Polishing canvas interactions that thousands of creatives touch every day — the small details users never explicitly notice but always feel.

You’ll work directly with senior engineers and the founders. Expect fast feedback, real code review, and more ownership than you’ve been trusted with before.

You’ll fit if you

- Are pursuing a degree in CS (or equivalent) and have built something real: a side project people actually used, open source contributions, a previous internship where you shipped.

- Are comfortable in TypeScript, or good enough at programming that you’ll be effective in it within a week.

- Have played with LLMs beyond the chat box. Tool-calling, agent frameworks, React Flow, Yjs/CRDTs, or anything you hacked together at 2am are all table stakes.

- Care about small details users never explicitly notice.

- Are comfortable with uncertainty. We might implode tomorrow or we might grow 100,000,000% WoW next week.

- Default to shipping. Let’s get shit done.

What we offer

- $8500 monthly salary

- $2500 monthly stipend for housing

- $70 per diem for meals

- In-person in NYC with a lean team of people who love the game, obsessed with building the future of creativity.

If this is the kind of problem you’re interested in, apply

About FSH

FSH Tech builds modern software that just works for the public sector. When we deliver, taxpayer dollars go further, agencies move faster, and millions of Americans get tangibly better service and quality of life.

Local governments, schools, libraries, and emergency services run on brittle software that was built decades ago. This results in wasted budgets, broken workflows, and bad outcomes for the public. We believe that the institutions closest to people's daily lives deserve products as good as anything in the private sector. We're building them.

We're a small, high-agency team. The people who do their best work here are:

- Relentlessly optimistic in creating a better world now

- Driven to maximize societal impact

- Brilliant and creative

About FSH Engineering

Our ideal candidate is an expert in their craft. They gain energy from understanding how their chosen tools work, and have used their tools to build software many times. Our ideal candidate is obsessively curious, motivated by customer outcomes, and is a technical artist.

We use Python, Postgres, Unix, TypeScript and React to build software. We maintain a set of internal tools to deterministically generate Python and Typescript. We obsess over how to build compounding advantages in tooling, software, and product. You don’t need to know our stack coming in. Strong fundamentals and fast learning matter more.

About the Internship

This is a 10-week paid internship opportunity.

We want to work with people who love to learn and do so quickly! Much of an engineer’s job involves learning by doing, and this is our pathway for those with less experience to do just that. You'll be building real projects for real customers.

Our work balances the deeply technical with the fundamentally human; we switch from technical architecture to design critique to product construction quickly. You will be paired with a senior engineer who focuses on mentorship. They'll help you set goals from the start, expand your scope and ownership, and pair with you often when you're stuck.

There is no predefined destination for this role and we don’t believe in having others do work we wouldn’t do ourselves (e.g. this isn’t a cover for ‘you will simply respond to tickets'). We want to help you ship customer value and will enable you to do so throughout your internship.

Strong interns will be considered for a full-time offer.

What You'll Do

- Build and maintain software for customers

- Seek and ingest feedback

- Iterate quickly

What You'll Need (optional)

- Experience shipping software to users

You’re the right person for the job if many of these are true:

- You believe programming is a creative pursuit

- You are a perennial tinkerer

- You gain energy from being close to the customer, always

- You are obsessed with focused learning

- You believe abstractions can simplify complexity

- You love pattern seeking, e.g.:

- Modern inventory management is best handled through Venetian double entry accounting

- Buddhist meditation and dialectical behavior therapy are closely related

- The distribution of crater sizes on the moon follow a power law

- Rivers and their tributaries, blood vessels, lunch bronchi, broccoli, and lightning bolts all demonstrate related patterns

Interns are expected to live in New York City or Philadelphia and work out of our office in either location.
